blocks.text: You can create notifications in the Zscaler Admin Console.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Alerts > Private Access.
The Notifications page appears.
Click Add.
On the Add Notification page:
General Information
On the General Information tab:
Name: Enter the name of the notification.
Status: The status of the notification (i.e., Enabled or Disabled). By default, the status is set to Enabled.
Component: Select a software component from the drop-down menu. The following software components are available:
App Connectors: To learn more, see About App Connectors.
Backup and Restore: To learn more, see About Backup and Restore.
Cloud Connectors: To learn more, see About Cloud Connectors.
Federation: To learn more, see Understanding Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation.
Network Connectors: To learn more, see About Network Connectors.
Private Cloud Controller: To learn more, see About Private Cloud Controllers.
Private Service Edges: To learn more, see About Private Service Edges.
VPN (for Legacy Apps): To learn more, see About VPN Service Edges.
Zscaler Client Connector: To learn more, see What Is Zscaler Client Connector?
If you are within a Microtenant, you can only create notifications for App Connectors, Private Service Edges for Private Access (ZPA), or Private Cloud Controllers.
After a component is selected, additional drop-down menus appear for Categories, Priorities, and selection of the components.
Select a component from the drop-down menu. You can search for a specific component or select an individual component in the drop-down menu. Click the selected component to remove it.
A drop-down menu for component selection is not available for Backup and Restore, Federation, and Zscaler Client Connector.

Categories: Select a category from the drop-down menu. You can select an individual category, click Select All to select all categories displayed in the drop-down menu, or click Remove All to remove all selections. All categories are selected by default. The following categories are available:
Backup Configuration: Indicates notifications regarding configuration backups and backups that are created manually or automatically.
Connectivity and Upgrade: Indicates notifications regarding the component connectivity and component upgrades.
Enrollment: Indicates notifications regarding the component enrollment.
Federated Application Configuration: Indicates events related to federated application configurations.
Federated Policy Configuration: Indicates events related to access policies for federated application configurations.
Partner Federation Configuration: Indicates events related to partner federation configurations.
System Resource: Indicates notifications regarding the component system resources.
Usage Metrics: Indicates notifications regarding the component usage metrics.
VPN (for Legacy Apps): Indicates notifications regarding the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) network routes and peers.

Priorities: Select the priority of the notification (i.e., Low, Medium, or High). You can select an individual priority, click Select All to select all priorities displayed in the drop-down menu, or click Remove All to remove all selections. All priorities are selected by default.
Click Next.
See image.
Events
On the Events tab:
Click Add Events.
Select the desired event.
For events that require text input, enter an integer value within the supported range. To learn more, see the following table.
View a list of events.
The following table provides a list of events, as well as the category and component the event belongs to:

table: An event indicating when the component's application count has exceeded the limit. The Application Exceeded Count Limit value must be an integer between 4500 and 6000. The default value is set to 4500.
An event indicating when the backup is completed. To learn more, see About Backup and Restore and Restoring Policies and Configurations from a Backup.
An event indicating when the backup has failed. To learn more, see About Backup and Restore and Restoring Policies and Configurations from a Backup.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges

An event indicating when the component's bandwidth utilization has exceeded the limit. The Bandwidth Utilization Exceeded Limit value must be an integer greater than or equal to 250 Mbps. The default value is set to 250.
An event indicating the number of BGP peers that have dropped from the Established state.
BGP Network Routes Peers Count Dropped
An event indicating the number of network sessions with BGP peers that have dropped or had routes withdrawn.
An event indicating that the session between BGP peers ended.
An event indicating that a BGP session has been down for an extended period of time.
An event indicating that a BGP peer session is unstable and repeatedly goes down and comes back up.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges
An event indicating when the control connection for a component disconnects.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, VPN Service Edges

An event indicating when the component's CPU utilization has exceeded the limit. The CPU Exceeded Limit value must be an integer between 75% and 99%. The default value is set to 75. To learn more, see Monitoring App Connector Performance and Monitoring Private Service Edge Performance.
App Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges
An event indicating when the component's CPU is missing resources needed for operations.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, VPN Service Edges

An event indicating when the component's available disk space is less than the indicated threshold. The Disk Space Exceeded Limit value must be an integer between 0 and 2048 MB. The default value is set to 2048. To learn more, see Monitoring App Connector Performance and Monitoring Private Service Edge Performance.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Service Edges
An event indicating when an enrollment certificate has expired for the selected component. To learn more, see About Enrollment (CA) Certificates.
App Connectors, Network Connectors,Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, Cloud Connectors
An event indicating when the enrollment of the component is completed.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Service Edges
An event indicating when the enrollment for the selected component has failed.
An event indicating when the configuration of the access policy for federated applications is created, updated, or deleted.
An event indicating when the configuration of the federated application is created, updated, or deleted.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, VPN Service Edges

An event indicating when the component's file descriptors are exhausted. The File Descriptors Exhausted value must be an integer between 75% and 99%. The default value is set to 75. To learn more, see Monitoring App Connector Performance and Monitoring Private Service Edge Performance.
Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges
An event indicating when the listen IP address configuration for a Private Service Edge or Private Cloud Controller is invalid.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges
An event indicating that all components in a group are disconnected.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges
An event indicating the Manager software version is outdated for the selected components.
An event indicating when the status of the partner federation is updated from Active, Pause, or Terminate.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, Cloud Connectors
An event indicating when the provisioning key has exceeded the limit for the selected components.
An event indicating when the restore is completed. To learn more, see About Backup and Restore and Restoring Policies and Configurations from a Backup.
An event indicating when the restore has failed. To learn more, see About Backup and Restore and Restoring Policies and Configurations from a Backup.
An event indicating when SCIM users are deleted successfully.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, VPN Service Edges
An event indicating when the component's source TCP or UDP ports are exhausted. The exhausted values must be an integer between 75% and 99%. The default value is set to 75.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, VPN Service Edges

An event indicating when the component's system memory has exceeded the limit. The System Memory Exceeded Limit value must be an integer between 75% and 99%. The default value is set to 75. To learn more, see Monitoring App Connector Performance and Monitoring Private Service Edge Performance.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges
An event indicating when an upgrade is complete for the selected components.
App Connectors, Network Connectors, Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges
An event indicating when an upgrade fails for the selected components.

Click Next.
Action
On the Action tab:
Throttling: By default, this setting is disabled. Select Enabled to enforce limits and timeout durations on a notification, and the following fields appear:
Throttling Limit: Enter an integer value to indicate the throttling limit.
Throttling Timeout: Enter an integer value in hours to indicate the throttling timeout.

For example, the Throttling Limit value is 3, and the Throttling Timeout value is 1 hour. If the notification is set to trigger when the App Connector CPU is greater than 80%, the recipients receive only three email notifications within the last hour if the CPU of the App Connector exceeds the 80% threshold.

Recipients: Select the recipients from the drop-down menu. You can search for a specific recipient, select an individual recipient, click Select All to select all recipients displayed in the drop-down menu, click Remove All to remove all selections, or click the Delete icon next to the selected recipient to remove it.
Distribution List: Enter the desired distribution list in the following format: example@test.com. Click Add so that the distribution list receives notifications after the notification is configured.
See an example email sent to a configured recipient.
Subject: [!] ZPA: Automatic Usage Metrics for Connector Lab App Connector with HIGH priority
Body: You are receiving this message because you requested notifications for:
Tenant Name: SafemarchTenant ID: 198745983939657747ZPA
Cloud Name: ProductionZPA
Component: App ConnectorName: Lab App Connector
Priority: HIGH
Event/Notification alert: Event triggered as a result of Memory exceeded
Review the relevant dashboards, analytics, and configuration settings in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Thank you,
Zscaler

The sender email domain for the notifications might come from no-reply@private.zscaler.com or no-reply@zpatwo.net depending on your organization's assigned cloud. To learn more, see Understanding Zscaler Cloud Names.
Click Next.
See image.
Review
Review your configured settings, and click Save.

blocks.text: Notifications that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be configured, edited, or deleted.

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Alerts > Private Access.
Locate the notification you want to edit, and click the Edit icon.
The Edit Notification page appears.
On the Edit Notification page, modify fields as necessary, and then continue the steps to edit a notification.
Go to Administration > Alerts > Private Access.
Locate the notification you want to copy, and click the Copy icon.
The Duplicate page appears that contains the prepopulated fields from the copied notification.
On the Duplicate page, modify fields as necessary, and then continue the steps to add the new notification.
